text:
maya: Heads-up — Halo customer reporting quality drop after merging their LoRA into rdx/gpt-large and quantizing to int4. Quick eval pack shows hallucinations on extractive QA. Can someone triage?
jon: @maya got it. Do we have the quick eval pack id and the exact command used to run the quantized artifact?
maya: pack id: halo_quick_v2. Command they used: ```
run_quick_eval --model rdx/gpt-large+halo-lora 
--quant int4 
--pack halo_quick_v2 
--seed 42
```
jon: thanks. I'll start a local replicate with the same flags. Any samples of failing prompts?
maya: pasted one snippet below — before (float16 merge) vs after (int4 merge):
---
INPUT: "Summarize the refund policy for order #A12345."
FLOAT16 OUTPUT: "Refunds issued within 30 days for damaged items. Contact support at support@example.com."
INT4 OUTPUT: "Refunds are processed by order number. See paragraph three for limits."
---
maya: it's paraphrasing away important specifics and occasionally hallucinating contact info.
rahul: smells like tokenization shift or merge folding artefact. Did customer use a different tokenizer or change normalize_whitespace? Even small tokenization diffs can flip alignment after quantization.
grace: can we check token counts? Maya, can you run `python -c "import t; print(len(tok.encode(p)))"` on a couple of failing prompts and compare pre/post merge?
maya: did that — token counts increased ~3-5% after applying the LoRA. Example: "Order number" tokenized as ["Order"," number"] vs previously a single token.
jon: running quick replicate now. ci-bot: starting smoke job on dedicated-small (slot 7).
ci-bot: smoke job 1745054360: baseline float16 pass; int4 run reported 12/50 tests failing (mainly QA and date extraction).
rahul: two quick suggestions: 1) try quant-aware merge (`tools/quant_merge --mode int4-safe`) which preserves per-channel scales; 2) try re-merging with bias-only fold to avoid weight folding that amplifies tokenization drift.
maya: tried quant_merge --mode int4-safe on a small subset — F1 regression dropped from 9% -> 2% on our QA microbench. Still need to run full pack.
liam: I can book a Dedicated slot for the full halo_quick_v2 pack tonight. ETA 3h.
grace: I'll add the pack to Console and set a canary route: prefer float16 with automatic fallback to float16 if int4 fails >3% delta.
jon: after liam runs the full pack, please attach the eval artifact here. We'll compare perplexity + QA F1 + exact-match.
maya: will do. If the regression persists after quant_merge, we may ask the customer for an 8-bit-friendly LoRA export or try a small tokenizer remap patch. :thinking_face:
rahul: also check if KV cache alignment differs — sometimes tokenization changes shift cached positions causing generation drift for long prompts.
maya: noted. Thanks all — appreciate the quick help. I'll post results from the full run when it's done. :thumbsup:
